stem: A parent is updating their 8-year-old's asthma action plan and asks which symptom is least reliable to use as the main trigger for escalation because children may not report it consistently?
explanation: Chest tightness is the correct answer. This is because children may not reliably describe chest tightness, so written asthma plans should rely more on observable signs of deterioration than on symptoms the child may not report consistently.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because children may not reliably describe chest tightness, making it a less dependable main trigger for escalation.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because tachypnoea is an observable sign of respiratory distress and is useful in assessing deterioration.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because accessory muscle use is an objective sign of increased work of breathing.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because lethargy is a concerning observable feature of illness and can indicate deterioration.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because wheeze is an important clinical sign of asthma, although it is not the least reliable symptom in this context.
